video_title: Better Buy: Marvell or Broadcom? | MRVL Stock vs. AVGO Stock

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: AI demand keeps exceeding supply, with products selling out years ahead.
claims.evidence_text: AI stocks are booming. Demand continues to exceed supply, and the more we go forward, the more products are selling out, the more years in the future.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Broadcom is poised to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom.
claims.evidence_text: So, it's understandable to be attracted to a lot of these AI companies, including Broadcom and Marvell, which are poised to be some of the biggest beneficiaries of this AI boom.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Marvell is poised to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom.
claims.evidence_text: So, it's understandable to be attracted to a lot of these AI companies, including Broadcom and Marvell, which are poised to be some of the biggest beneficiaries of this AI boom.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Broadcom sales grew from about $35 billion (early 2024) to about $90 billion trailing, helped by AI demand and VMware.
claims.evidence_text: And looking at it this way, Broadcom is demonstrating phenomenal sales and phenomenal growth. Its business boomed from around $35 billion in sales in early 2024 up to roughly $90 billion in sales over the trailing 12-month period.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Jensen Huang suggested Marvell could become the next trillion-dollar semiconductor company (its market cap is under 300 billion).
claims.evidence_text: Marvell's demand for its products and services are also soaring, and that led Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to suggest that Marvell could become the next trillion-dollar semiconductor company.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Long-term contracts give demand visibility for Broadcom and Marvell through 2027 and probably the first half of 2028; beyond 2028 question marks appear.
claims.evidence_text: Needless to say, demand for these companies' products and services are soaring, and they're likely to continue to be so at least for this year, the rest of next year, and then starting in 2028, probably the first half of 2028.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Broadcom's operating margin rose to 48.6% from about 5% in 2017.
claims.evidence_text: And in this regard, they're both experiencing significant improvement with Broadcom's operating profit margin soaring to 48.6%. That's up from around 5% in 2017.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Marvell's operating margin is 16.8%, about a third of Broadcom's, but improving.
claims.evidence_text: Marvell, meanwhile, is generating a fraction of this operating margin, roughly 1/3 at 16.8%, but Marvell's operating margin is improving as well.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: As the smaller Marvell grows, economies of scale can expand its profitability.
claims.evidence_text: As we saw earlier, Marvell is a much smaller scale business, so it's reasonable to assume as it grows larger, its profitability can expand further as it benefits from economies in scale.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Although growth comes from the lower-margin semiconductor segment, Broadcom's overall operating margin should stay at or above current levels.
claims.evidence_text: That being said, Broadcom's growth is coming more from its semiconductor segment, which generates lower profit margins than its software segment. Still, its profit margins in that segment are enough to keep the company's overall operating profit margin at or above the levels it's currently at.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Broadcom's ROIC is 25.75%, more than twice its cost of capital.
claims.evidence_text: Broadcom's ROIC has been impressive 25.75% more recently. That's more than two times the company's weighted average cost of capital.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Marvell's ROIC of 12.61% barely covers its cost of capital, about half of Broadcom's.
claims.evidence_text: Meanwhile, Marvell at 12.61% is barely at the company's weighted average cost of capital and roughly half that of Broadcom.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Marvell trades at 39x forward earnings, more than double Broadcom's 18x.
claims.evidence_text: Marvell is trading at a forward price to earnings of 39. That's more than double Broadcom's valuation on the same metric of 18.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Revenue, margins and ROIC all favor Broadcom, yet it trades at the cheaper valuation.
claims.evidence_text: And so, it's surprising to me that Broadcom is selling at a cheaper valuation, but I can understand why that's the case.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Marvell's premium reflects larger future growth prospects from a smaller base (under $300 billion vs Broadcom's 1.6 trillion).
claims.evidence_text: Now, it's my view that the reason Marvell is trading at a more premium valuation is because its growth prospects in future years are larger than Broadcom.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Better near-term growth does not justify Marvell's more than 2x valuation premium to Broadcom.
claims.evidence_text: And so, for that reason, investors are placing a premium on Marvell because its near-term growth prospects are better than Broadcom. But, does it deserve a more than 2x premium to Broadcom? I'm not so convinced of that fact.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: His discounted cash flow model puts Broadcom's fair value at 523 versus 353, roughly 48% upside.
claims.evidence_text: I calculated a fair value at 523. The current market price is 353. So, I calculate an upside of roughly 48% over the next 12 to 18 months for Broadcom.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: His discounted cash flow model puts Marvell's fair value at 207 versus 266, about 22% downside.
claims.evidence_text: Marvell, meanwhile, I calculated a fair value of 207. The current market price is 266. So, I calculated downside of 22% over the next 12 to 18 months for Marvell.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Micron's September 30 quarterly report will tell investors more about the AI industry.
claims.evidence_text: But, of course, we're going to learn more about the AI industry when Micron reports quarterly results on September 30th.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Answering 'Better Buy: Marvell or Broadcom?': given the valuation gap he prefers Broadcom.
claims.evidence_text: Given the differences in valuation, however, I would prefer Broadcom over Marvell.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Host owns Broadcom stock.
claims.evidence_text: And that's precisely the choice I made for my portfolio. I own Broadcom stock.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Host does not own Marvell stock.
claims.evidence_text: I don't own Marvell stock.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Not interested in buying Marvell anywhere near current levels; prefers Broadcom and several other semiconductor stocks.
claims.evidence_text: I'm not interested in buying Marvell stock anywhere near these levels.
